exposure: Delivery method (vaginal delivery, intrapartum cesarean delivery, elective cesarean delivery)
outcome: Postpartum pelvic floor function (POP-Q score, urinary incontinence incidence, pelvic floor muscle strength, PFDI-20 score)
cohort: Chinese primiparous women who delivered a full-term, cephalic, singleton infant
finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, elective cesarean delivery was associated with better pelvic floor function postpartum.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean delivery (ECD) was associated with a lower risk of pelvic organ prolapse and urinary incontinence, stronger pelvic floor muscle strength, and lower PFDI-20 scores compared to vaginal delivery.
